purpose: written for (the use of) Subbā Pravala Rāṇā
notes: The catalogue gives ŚS 1789, but the colophon reads 'śrīśāke 1719' (= 1797 CE, Mārgaśīrṣa, so Nov./Dec. 1797). The 1719 reading fits the Gorkha occupation of Kumaon (1790–1815), when a Subbā (governor) Prabal Rāṇā would be plausible, so the catalogue figure is probably a misprint. 'Pravala' is probably Prabala/Prabal. 'Yogyeṣu likhitam' means 'written for (the use of)': it makes him the owner/beneficiary and probably the commissioner. The colophon does not support the catalogue's 'Donor'. Gaṃgāvālī = Gaṅgolī in Kumaon. The colophon gives it as the scribe's residence ('nivāsinā'), not explicitly as the place of copying. Paṃta = Pant, a Kumaoni brahmin surname. Vaṅgasena (son of Gadādhara) is the author of the text.
